newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Russia sign $7.0 billion dollar gas deal.
newsitem.headline: China, Russia sign $7.0 billion dollar gas deal.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his Chinese counterpart Li Peng presided on Friday over the signing of a $7.0 billion dollar deal to supply China with natural gas from Siberia.
Under the deal, Russia would export 25 billion cubic metres of natural gas a year from its Kovyktinsky field in the Irkutsk region over the next 30 years, sources said.
Russian and Chinese officials in Beijing declined to say how much the deal was worth, but sources close to the Russian delegation put its value at about $7.0 billion.
The field would be tapped by Rusia Petroleum that groups Russia's SIDANCO oil firm and South Korea's East Asia Gas Co Ltd, a member of the Hanbo Group.
"South Korea will join the project in the form of some kind of construction and will share some of the financial debt," one Russian source said.
The deal called for Sino-Russian cooperation in building a huge pipeline to link the field with northeastern China, a Russian diplomat said.
"All the details are still under negotiations and this is just a framework agreement," the Russian source said.

The deal was signed by Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is also minister of fuel and energy, and an official of China's state-run China National Petroleum Corp, the diplomat said, but gave no further details.
Russian and Chinese officials also signed a 25-year, $1.5 billion deal to supply northeastern China with electricity, the source said.
Russia would supply much of the transmission equipment for the 2,000-km line while China would likely provide most of the financing, the source said.
The power project would supply 20 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity from Irkutsk to either Shenyang in China's northeast province of Liaoning or to Beijing, he said but gave no further details.
